column1: # gates/baseline.tsv — the ratchet baseline for scripts/gate-ratchet.sh
# (deterministic-gates §6: "Existing violations are recorded in a committed
# baseline. The gate fails if the count GOES UP; it never requires me to fix
# the past.")
# Format: <gate_id><TAB><command><TAB><violations><TAB><suppressions><TAB><recorded_at><TAB><note>
# The command is run from the repo root and MUST support --count, printing
# "<violations>TAB<suppressions>" on stdout and exiting 0. A command that exits
# 2 fails the ratchet as a gate error — never as a pass.
# SUPPRESSIONS ARE VIOLATIONS. A declared standalone, a nolint pragma, a scope
# exclusion — each counts in the second number. That is the whole anti-bypass
# design: routing around a gate moves a number that is watched, so it can never
# be the quiet option. §6 again: "If suppression does not enter the ratchet, you
# will route around the gate instead of obeying it — and I want that to be
# impossible, not merely discouraged."
# TO LOWER A NUMBER: fix the violations, then edit the row. Downward is silent.
# TO RAISE A NUMBER: you must edit this file deliberately and say why in the
# note. That edit is the artifact — it shows up in review as a decision, not as
# an accident.
# EVERY gate in scripts/, gates/ and context/gates/ must have a row here. A gate
# with no row is a violation, not a skip — otherwise a new gate escapes the
# ratchet simply by never being registered.
# gates/ is named explicitly because it is where /ctx-gate writes every gate it
# builds (scripts/new-gate.sh). It was missing from the check until 2026-08-08,
# which meant the first gate the compiler generated for itself was exempt from
# the requirement this paragraph states. Pinned by the fixture pair
# tests/gates/ratchet/gates-arm-dirty -> tests/gates/ratchet/clean.
# ONE EXCEPTION, and it is structural: scripts/gate-ratchet.sh has no row. It is
# the only gate with no --count mode, because "count your own violations" is not
# defined for the script that reads this file — and a row naming it would make
# it invoke itself once per run, forever. It is fixtured like every other gate
# instead (two pairs in scripts/gate-fixtures.tsv), so its coverage does not
# depend on a number nobody could compute.
# gate_id
